title: Japanese for Shopping in 9 Comic Scenes | Guess, Listen, Say It (Travel Japanese)
lead: Browsing, trying things on, sizes and colours, tax-free, gift wrapping and bags, everything for shopping in Japan in nine comic scenes. Guess first, then listen twice and say it.

intro.title:
Japan shopping
**9 phrases**
intro.say: Nine scenes in a Japanese clothes shop. Guess each line before the answer.

phrases.label: Just looking
phrases.when: If a clerk asks what you are looking for and you are only browsing, answer like this.
phrases.tip: Say it with a smile and the staff will let you browse in peace.
phrases.hear: 何かお探しですか？ (Nanika osagashi desu ka?) = Are you looking for something?
phrases.short: When a shop clerk talks to you in Japan
phrases.scene: Between clothing racks, Jiwoo browses a rail of sweaters; the clerk approaches from the right with a helpful smile, and Jiwoo answers with a friendly little wave; Minjun looks at jackets behind her.

phrases.label: Other colours
phrases.ja: ほかの色はありますか？
phrases.pron: Hoka no iro wa arimasu ka?
phrases.when: Like it but want a different colour? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Black is kuro, white is shiro. You can ask kuro wa arimasu ka.
phrases.scene: Jiwoo holds up a mustard-coloured sweater and points at it with a questioning look; the clerk on the right holds up the same sweater folded in indigo and grey.

phrases.label: Trying it on
phrases.ja: 試着してもいいですか？
phrases.pron: Shichaku shite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.when: Want to try something on? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Shichaku means trying on. In many shops you take your shoes off before stepping into the fitting room.
phrases.scene: Jiwoo holds the indigo sweater against her body and points toward a fitting room with a curtain; the clerk nods and gestures toward it with an open hand.

phrases.label: A bigger size
phrases.ja: もっと大きいサイズはありますか？
phrases.pron: Motto ookii saizu wa arimasu ka?
phrases.ko: Do you have a bigger size?
phrases.tip: Smaller is motto chiisai saizu. Japanese sizes can run a little small.
phrases.scene: Jiwoo peeks out from the fitting room curtain, the sweater sleeves too short on her arms, and asks the clerk waiting outside on the right; Minjun laughs in the background.

phrases.label: I'll take it
phrases.tip: You can use the same phrase when choosing from a menu.
phrases.scene: Now wearing a sweater that fits, Jiwoo stands in front of a mirror and gives a happy thumbs-up, holding the sweater out to the clerk.

phrases.label: Tax-free
phrases.when: At the checkout, ask if you can buy it tax-free.
phrases.tip: Now you pay the tax at the till and get it back at airport customs when you leave Japan. Bring your actual passport.
phrases.scene: At the checkout counter, Jiwoo holds out her passport with both hands and asks the clerk behind the counter, the folded sweater between them.

phrases.label: Gift wrapping
phrases.ja: プレゼント用に包んでもらえますか？
phrases.ko: Could you wrap it as a gift?
phrases.when: Buying a gift? Ask for wrapping like this.
phrases.tip: Purezento-you means for a present. Many shops will wrap it for you.
phrases.scene: At the counter, Jiwoo holds a small plain box and mimes tying a ribbon with her fingers; the clerk smiles and holds up a sheet of plain wrapping paper.

phrases.label: Separate bags
phrases.ja: 袋を分けてもらえますか？
phrases.ko: Could you put them in separate bags?
phrases.when: Want the gift in a separate bag? Ask this.
phrases.tip: If you don't need a bag, say fukuro wa irimasen. Some shops charge for bags.
phrases.scene: At the counter, Jiwoo points at the sweater and then at the wrapped gift box, holding her hands apart; the clerk holds up two plain paper shopping bags.

bonus.label: When you leave
bonus.when: Finally, say this as you leave the shop. The staff will love it.
bonus.scene: At the shop door, Jiwoo holds two paper shopping bags and waves happily; Minjun carries another bag; the clerk bows on the right.

outro.title: Recap: **9 phrases**
outro.say: All the phrases are in the description. Tell us in the comments how many you got right. Subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
